arms.name: M-ESCAPES-TRUTH-FACTS
arms.replace: if (view != null && view.truth && false) return factsAnswer(view);
arms.note: under the truth the escapes are still read off the project's syntax, which counts every value handed to library code as escaped

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-REFLECTION-INLINED
arms.note: any reflective body spliced in is taken to produce a class from a name it lost, so the escapes are never known

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-FLOW
arms.note: a value flowing into a catch-all, a type parameter, a structure or through a cast is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-HANDED
arms.find: for (h in n.handed) if (!typeParameter(h.to) && !escape(h.from)) return false;
arms.note: a value handed to target code is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-CLOSURE
arms.note: the receiver of a method read as a value is taken to stay in the type system, though the bound function carries it

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-DYNAMIC-RECEIVER
arms.note: the receiver of a field reached by name in untyped code is taken to stay in the type system, though any of its fields may be read

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PRODUCED
arms.note: a class a class-value producer names is taken never to be instantiated untyped

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-INSTANCES
arms.find:
if (fact != null && fact.params.length == args.length) for (i => name in fact.params)
				bindInstance(out, '$id.$name', args[i]);
arms.note: a type written with arguments binds nothing, so a value a generic class lets go is of no type

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PARAMETER
arms.find: if (bound != null) for (x in bound) if (!escapeType(x)) return false;
arms.note: a value of a type parameter is taken to be of no type, so what its instantiations bind it to never escapes

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-GENERIC-METHOD
arms.note: the instantiation of a generic method binds nothing, so a value it lets go is of no type

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-EXTENDS-EXTERN
arms.note: an instance of a class extending an extern is taken to stay in the type system, though target code runs with it as `this`

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-FIELDS
arms.find: for (f in currentFact.fields) if (f.kinds.exists(k -> k.startsWith('var(')) && !within(f.types, currentBound)) return false;
arms.note: what an escaped object's variables hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-ENUM
arms.find: case 'enum': fact.constructors.foreach(c -> constructorEscapes(id, c.name, c.type, bound));
arms.note: what an escaped enum value's constructor arguments hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-STRUCTURE
arms.note: what an escaped structure's fields hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PLACE-ARGS
arms.note: a place of a nominal type is taken to keep the type of what it holds whatever its arguments, `Array<Dynamic>` included

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-TYPE-ARGS
arms.note: what an escaped container holds by its type arguments, which no variable of it declares, is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-SUBTYPES
arms.note: an escaped value is taken to be of exactly its static class, never one of its subtypes

arms.name: M-REACH-EXACT-SITE
arms.find: at.exact ? exactTypes(g, t) : runtimeTypes(g, t, at.family)
arms.note: an object built right at a conversion site may be any subtype of its class, or any escaped instance

arms.name: M-FACTS-VIEW-EXACT
arms.note: the exactness the facts record of a converted operand is dropped

arms.name: M-FACTS-VIEW-EXACT-CONVERSION
arms.note: the exactness the facts record of the argument of a conversion call is dropped

arms.name: M-FACTS-FLOW-EXACT
arms.note: the exactness of a value flowing whole is recorded nowhere

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-JOINED-CONVERSION
arms.note: a conversion the compiler writes of a field read it placed across an inlined body and the text is no text's (the client's `model.Node.parse`)

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-JOINED-PLACED
arms.note: the value a field read the compiler placed across an inlined body and the text flows as is no text's (the client's `model.Node.parse`)

arms.name: M-FACTS-TREE-OPTIONAL
arms.note: a lone `?` argument is read as an optional argument, so an unknown argument type reads as a malformed type

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-WALK
arms.find: reachedArrayChange(g, file, tree, region, callees, shared);
arms.note: what a shared collection's region calls is admitted unwalked, so a callee growing any array proves

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-REFUSED
arms.note: every call a shared collection's region makes is a culprit again, so a region calling a pure project function is refused

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-BENIGN-EDGE
arms.note: a callee's push onto a fresh local of its own is followed into the built-in array type, whose body-less mutator refuses

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-REWRITTEN
arms.note: a callee a build macro may rewrite is read as its source

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-AMBIGUOUS
arms.note: a callee whose type name two declarations share is read as one of them

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-OVERRIDES
arms.note: a dispatch on a library type reaches only the declaration, not the overrides library code declares

arms.name: M-REACH-COMPOUND-WRITE-ALIAS
arms.find: final replacing: Bool = write.kind == shape.assignKind || write.kind == shape.nullCoalAssignKind;
arms.replace:
final replacing: Bool = true;
		if (write.kind != shape.assignKind) return true;
arms.note: only a plain assignment of a shared value is an escape, so `x ??= shared` leaves `x` a fresh local whose push is taken as harmless

arms.name: M-REACH-ASSIGNMENT-VALUE-ALIAS
arms.replace: if (true) return holder.kind != shape.exprStatementKind || valueDiscarded(lineage, at - 1);
arms.note: an assignment used as a value keeps its target fresh, so `all = xs = [1]` leaves `xs` unshared though `all` holds it

arms.name: M-REACH-LAST-STATEMENT-VALUE
arms.replace: final climbs: Bool = true || kind == shape.blockStmtKind
arms.note: every construct a statement ends is climbed as if its value were discarded, so `all = { xs = [1]; }` keeps `xs` unshared

arms.name: M-REACH-DISCARDED-BODY
arms.note: a loop's body is not taken as discarding its last statement's value, so a fresh write ending a loop body makes the local shared

arms.name: M-REACH-DISCARDED-STATEMENT-BRANCH
arms.note: no statement branch or nested block is climbed, so a fresh write ending an `if` / `switch` statement branch makes the local shared

arms.name: M-ORACLE-PARALLEL-HALF-THE-CORES
arms.note: the compile budget is half the cores again, so a thirteen-configuration project compiles in four waves on a sixteen-core machine

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-PROBE-RECOMPILES
arms.find: final held: Array<Null<HaxeRun>> = [for (i in 0...asked.length) memo?.run(asked[i], true, before[i])];
arms.note: the coverage probe compiles the tree its baseline just compiled with -v, paying a second compile per configuration

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-KEY-IGNORES-CONTENT
arms.note: a remembered verdict answers for any content of the tree, so an edit that breaks the build is judged by the verdict of the tree before it

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-QUOTES-THE-VERBOSE-STREAMS
arms.find: final retried: Array<Int> = [for (k in 0...runs.length) if (answered(runs[k]) && runs[k].status != 0) k];
arms.note: a failing -v baseline is quoted with its -v lines, so a rejection's text names every parsed file

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-FILES-A-MOVED-INPUT
arms.note: a compile whose input changed while it ran is filed under the content it started from, so that content is later answered with a verdict about another

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-NO-BASELINE-AHEAD
arms.note: the facts compile no longer brings the baseline along, so the baseline asked next is a compile of its own

arms.name: M-PENDING-RUNS-IN-FOREGROUND
arms.find: final answer: Array<HaxeRun> = pid == null ? HaxeSpawn.runAll(_jobs, _maxBuffer, _parallel, false, _bound) : collect(pid);
arms.note: a background batch is run again in the foreground when it is awaited, so nothing it did while the caller worked is saved

arms.name: M-PENDING-CANCEL-LEAVES-JOBS
arms.note: a cancelled batch leaves its driver running, so the jobs it started run to their end after the run abandoned them

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-NOT-ATTACHED
arms.find: return OracleRunMemo.attach(prepared.oracles, new OracleRunMemo(persisted, () -> [for (f in files) f.file]));
arms.note: a lint run's configurations carry no memo, so every phase compiles the tree it asks about again

arms.name: M-FACTS-NEVER-EARLY
arms.note: no run starts its facts compiles ahead, so they follow the first check that asks instead of overlapping the checks

arms.name: M-FACTS-EARLY-DIRS-LEFT
arms.note: facts compiles no check asked for leave their probe directories behind

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-WRITTEN-UNHASHED
arms.note: the run's fingerprint rests on the library directories hashed earlier in the process, so an edit to a project whose sources arrive through -lib leaves it unchanged and the verification is answered from the baseline

arms.name: M-RUNMEMO-TRUSTS-UNSEEN-SOURCES
arms.note: a configuration that reads files outside every directory its fingerprint walks is answered from the memo, so an edit there reuses a verdict about the old content

arms.name: M-PENDING-JOBS-FILE-KEPT
arms.note: the driver leaves the job list in its directory, so a run killed mid-batch leaves the job list behind

arms.name: M-DSN-UNSEEN-DROPPED
arms.note: no narrowing is ever marked invisible to the compiler, so dead-safe-nav rewrites a Bool-local / alias / `?.`-comparison proof to `.` under null-safety and the build breaks

arms.name: M-DSN-UNSEEN-ALL
arms.note: a direct `== null` / `!= null` guard counts as invisible too, so dead-safe-nav declines the fix the compiler would accept

arms.name: M-DSN-NULLSAFE-ALWAYS
arms.note: plain code is treated as null-checked, so a runtime-sound Bool-local proof loses its fix (dead-safe-nav, dead-null-guard, dead-null-coalescing) where nothing typechecks it

arms.name: M-DSN-JOIN-EITHER
arms.note: a join forgets that one arm proved the name only invisibly, so the fix lands on a path the compiler never narrowed

arms.name: M-DSN-RENARROW-HIDES
arms.note: an invisible re-narrowing hides a proof the compiler already has, so an accepted fix is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-ASSIGN-KEEPS-UNSEEN
arms.note: a non-null assignment no longer makes the proof visible, so the fix after `x = new T()` is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-MACRO-BLIND
arms.note: a project-wide `--macro nullSafety` in the oracle hxml is ignored, so a meta-free module gets the `.` rewrite its build rejects

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-ALWAYS-ON
arms.note: every oracle build reads as enabling null-safety, so a plain project loses the runtime-sound fix

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-COMMENT-READ
arms.note: a commented-out `#--macro nullSafety` is read as live, so the fix is declined in a plain build

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-LIB-PLAIN
arms.note: a `-lib` is taken as plain although its extraParams may add `@:nullSafety`, so the build-breaking fix lands

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-INCLUDE-SKIPPED
arms.note: an included hxml is never read, so a `nullSafety` macro in it goes unseen and the build-breaking fix lands

arms.name: M-DSN-HXML-UNREADABLE-PLAIN
arms.note: an oracle hxml not generated yet reads as plain, so the fix lands before the build that may reject it exists

arms.name: M-DSN-TRY-KEEPS-ALL
arms.note: a proof made inside a `try` stays visible past it, so the `.` rewrite after the try does not compile

arms.name: M-DSN-TRY-HIDES-ALL
arms.find: final kept: Array<String> = visibleUnwritten(state, node, ctx);
arms.note: a proof made before a `try` is hidden past it, so an accepted fix is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-LONE-ARM-KEEPS-BODY
arms.note: what the body of a lone surviving `if` arm proved stays visible past the `if`, so the `.` rewrite does not compile

arms.name: M-DSN-LONE-ARM-HIDES-ALL
arms.find: final elseKept: Array<String> = elseArm == null ? visibleIn(elseState) : visibleUnwritten(elseState, elseArm, ctx);
arms.note: the condition's own narrowing is hidden past a lone surviving arm, so the fix after `if (x == null || b) return;`-style guards is declined

arms.name: M-DSN-JOIN-HIDES-ALL
arms.note: every join hides its proof, so two live arms that each narrow visibly lose their fix

arms.name: M-DSN-LONE-BRANCH-KEEPS-BODY
arms.note: what a lone live `switch` branch proved stays visible past the switch, so the `.` rewrite does not compile

arms.name: M-DSN-OWNS-NONE
arms.note: no construct keeps what its children proved, so an assignment inside a call argument loses a fix the compiler accepts

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-BINDER-BLIND
arms.find: final bound: Array<String> = ctx.selfScopeDeclKinds.contains(kind) ? boundNames(node, ctx) : [];
arms.note: a loop binder no longer shadows the outer name, so the outer non-null proof reaches `x?.f` on the binder and the fix / dead-fallback deletion crashes at runtime on a null element

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-CHILD-BINDER-BLIND
arms.note: a key-value loop's VALUE binder no longer shadows, so `for (k => x in m)` inherits the outer `x` proof

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-CASE-BINDER-BLIND
arms.note: a case capture no longer shadows, so `case x:` / `case var x:` inherit the outer proof

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-CATCH-BINDER-BLIND
arms.note: a catch variable no longer shadows, so `catch (x:Dynamic)` inherits the outer proof

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-SHADOW-NO-RESTORE
arms.note: the outer fact is never restored past a shadowing scope, so the fix after the loop is lost

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-SHADOW-RESTORES-WRITTEN
arms.note: the outer fact is restored even when the construct writes the name, so a null written by the iterable is read as non-null

arms.name: M-NULLITY-ALIAS-TRUSTED
arms.note: a typedef proves non-null by being one, so `typedef MaybeR = Null<R>` reads as a plain nominal again

arms.name: M-NULLITY-UNDERLYING-TRUSTED
arms.replace: if (_nominalKinds.contains(t.kind) || t.isAnonStruct || t.underlyingRaw != null) return NonNull;
arms.note: an abstract proves non-null whatever it wraps, so one over `Null<R>` is trusted

arms.name: M-NULLITY-TYPE-PARAMS-IGNORED
arms.find: if (head == null || hops > MAX_HOPS || typeParams.contains(head)) return Unproven;
arms.replace: if (head == null || hops > MAX_HOPS) return Unproven;
arms.note: a type parameter of the declaration a hop reaches resolves to whatever same-named type is in scope, so `typedef Id<T> = T` borrows class `T`'s proof

arms.name: M-NULLITY-BINDING-PARAMS-DROPPED
find: if (typeName == null || isTypeParamAt(typeName, bindingFrom)) return Unproven;
arms.note: the type parameters in scope at a binding are not, so `m<R>(x:R)` borrows class `R`'s proof

arms.name: M-NULLITY-UNRESOLVED-PROVEN
arms.note: a name that resolves to nothing is proven by the empty agreement

arms.name: M-NULLITY-GUARD-IGNORED
arms.note: a `#if`-guarded declaration answers for every branch, though the index kept only one

arms.name: M-NULLITY-HOPS-CUT
arms.note: no alias or underlying type is followed, so an alias of a class or an abstract over one proves nothing

arms.name: M-NULLITY-ANON-REFUSED
arms.note: an anonymous-structure typedef proves nothing, though a structure value is non-null under null safety

arms.name: M-NULLITY-SCOPE-LOST
arms.note: names resolve from no file, so an imported class stops proving anything

arms.name: M-PROVER-NULLITY-SKIPPED
arms.note: the null-safety arm trusts any declared nominal again, so a typedef of `Null<…>` is rewritten by every null-aware check

arms.name: M-VALUE-TYPE-UNINIT-FIELD
arms.note: a value-typed field with no initialiser keeps the fast path, though it reads null on a dynamic target until assigned

arms.name: M-VALUE-TYPE-FIELDS-REFUSED
arms.note: every value-typed field loses the fast path, an initialised one and one read through its getter included

arms.name: M-INTERP-NULLITY-SKIPPED
arms.note: any annotated identifier is interpolation-safe, a typedef of `Null<…>` included

arms.name: M-TOSTRING-RETURN-TRUSTED
arms.note: an instance call's declared return is trusted by name under null safety, so a method returning a typedef of `Null<…>` loses its `.toString()`

arms.name: M-ENTRY-POINT-UNREACHED
arms.note: `static function main()` is an ordinary private method, so `unused-private` deletes the program's entry point

arms.name: M-ENTRY-POINT-ANY-ARITY
arms.note: a `main` taking parameters counts as the entry point, which the compiler never calls

arms.name: M-CTOR-CLASS-VALUE-BLIND
arms.note: a class handed around as a value is still never-instantiated, so the constructor `Type.createInstance` runs is deleted

arms.name: M-CTOR-RECEIVER-AS-VALUE
arms.note: a static access `U.K` counts as a class value, so no utility class's private constructor is reported

arms.name: M-CTOR-ALIAS-BLIND
arms.note: a typedef aliasing the class is ignored, so a class value spelled by the alias reaches a deleted constructor

arms.name: M-BINDING-ALIAS-BLIND
arms.note: an import alias never binds its alias name, so a same-package class answers for `import other.Opt as MaybeR`

arms.name: M-BINDING-UNINDEXED-IMPORT-FREE
arms.note: an import or alias of a module nothing can read is taken to declare nothing, so it falls through to the package tier

arms.name: M-BINDING-UNINDEXED-MODULE-FREE
arms.find: if (split.rest.length > 1 || (!aliased && split.rest.length == 1 && split.rest[0] != name)) return Pass;
arms.replace: if (split.rest.length > 1 || (!aliased && split.rest.length == 1 && split.rest[0] != name) || (!aliased && split.rest.length == 0 && SourceText.lastSegment(split.module) != name && !tables().modules.exists(split.module))) return Pass;
arms.note: an unindexed module import is taken to declare no sub-type of the name

arms.name: M-BINDING-UNINDEXED-WILDCARD-FREE
arms.note: a wildcard over a package nothing can read is taken to bind nothing

arms.name: M-BINDING-OWN-TIER-CUT
arms.find: if (own.length > 0) return Bound([for (t in own) { file: fi, type: t }]);
arms.note: the module's own types are not asked first, so an import answers for a name the module itself declares

arms.name: M-BINDING-WILDCARD-CUT
arms.note: no wildcard import binds anything

arms.name: M-BINDING-PACKAGE-TIER-CUT
arms.note: no package or toplevel type binds anything

arms.name: M-BINDING-FIRST-STATEMENT-WINS
arms.note: the FIRST statement binding a name wins, explicit and wildcard alike, though the compiler asks the last one first

arms.name: M-BINDING-PRIVATE-VISIBLE
arms.note: a private type is read as imported by its module's import and visible to its package

arms.name: M-BINDING-SUBTYPES-VISIBLE
arms.note: a package wildcard is read as binding every type of the package's modules, sub-types included

arms.name: M-BINDING-ROOT-SUBTYPES
arms.note: a sub-type of a package or root module is read as visible by its bare name from the package

arms.name: M-BINDING-STDTYPES-CUT
arms.note: the types the compiler imports from `StdTypes` bind nothing, so a same-package namesake answers for `Iterable`

arms.name: M-BINDING-FIELD-IMPORT-UNKNOWN
arms.find: if (split.rest.length > 1 || (!aliased && split.rest.length == 1 && split.rest[0] != name)) return Pass;
arms.note: a static-field import, and a sub-type import of another name, are read as possibly binding the name

arms.name: M-BINDING-OUTSIDE-UNREAD
arms.note: no module outside the index is read, so a std import makes every name it does not bind unknown

arms.name: M-BINDING-STD-WILDCARD-BLIND
arms.note: a wildcard over a std package that has no module of the name is read as possibly binding it

arms.name: M-BINDING-GUARDED-OTHER-BUILD
arms.note: a guarded statement is unknown even where no other build binds the name

arms.name: M-BINDING-STRICT-OUTSIDE
arms.note: in a guarded statement's other build a package or toplevel module outside the index binds nothing, so the guarded binding is pinned against a std type the other build picks

arms.name: M-BINDING-COGUARD-IGNORED
arms.note: a use inside a guarded import's own branch is weighed against the build without the import, which never compiles it — openfl's `#if !flash` DisplayObject loses its supertype

arms.name: M-BINDING-STRICT-UNREAD-PASS
arms.note: in a guarded statement's other build a module nothing reads is taken as absent — the guess the binding exists to refuse

arms.name: M-COND-WITHIN-BRANCH-IGNORED
arms.note: a position in the `#else` of a region reads as inside its `#if` branch, so a use the build WITHOUT the import compiles is pinned to the import

arms.name: M-SCOPE-MODULE-TYPES-NONE
arms.note: the resolution scope never answers which types a module outside the index declares, so a library import makes every name it does not bind unknown

arms.name: M-SCOPE-ROOT-MODULE-ANYWHERE
arms.note: a file named after a module is taken for it whatever package it declares, so a ROOT module is found in any directory

arms.name: M-HAXELIB-BATCH-COUNT-IGNORED
arms.note: a multi-name `haxelib libpath` answer missing a line is read positionally, so every library after the gap takes its neighbour's root

arms.name: M-CTOR-IMPORT-ALIAS-BLIND
arms.note: an import alias of the class is not a spelling of it, so `Type.createInstance(K, [])` reaches a deleted constructor

arms.name: M-CTOR-QUALIFIED-BLIND
arms.note: a qualified path to the class is not a class value, so `Type.createInstance(pkg.U, [])` reaches a deleted constructor

arms.name: M-EFFECTIVE-IGNORES-CONFIG
arms.note: the listing reads the registry defaults and never the config, so a disabled rule is reported as run

arms.name: M-EFFECTIVE-IGNORES-DEFAULT-OFF
arms.note: an opt-in rule no config enables is listed as on

arms.name: M-EFFECTIVE-IGNORES-VERSION
arms.find: final gated: Bool = enabled && minimum != null && !config.allowsLanguageVersion(minimum);
arms.note: a rule whose findings the languageVersion gate drops is listed as on

arms.name: M-EFFECTIVE-GROUPS-PER-DIR
arms.note: two directories under one chain are listed as two groups

arms.name: M-CHAIN-NEAREST-ONLY
arms.note: the nearest apqlint.json replaces its ancestors instead of extending them

arms.name: M-CHAIN-IGNORES-INHERIT
arms.note: a document declaring inherit:false still folds its ancestors

arms.name: M-CHAIN-UNBOUNDED
arms.note: the chain climbs past the project root and folds a stray ancestor document

arms.name: M-GATE-COLLECT-BYPASS
arms.note: the run ignores the FileGated answer the listing reports, so an excluded file is scanned

arms.name: M-GATE-TS-SINKS-BLIND
arms.note: thread-safety without sinks is reported as running

arms.name: M-GATE-TS-EXCLUDE-BLIND
arms.note: a thread-safety exclude path is reported as scanned

arms.name: M-GATE-AD-EXCLUDE-BLIND
arms.note: an avoid-dynamic excludePaths file is reported as scanned

arms.name: M-GATE-NOOP-DOC
arms.note: doc-coverage asking for no docs is reported as running

arms.name: M-GATE-NOOP-UNDERSCORE
arms.note: no-underscore-prefix exempting params and locals is reported as running

arms.name: M-EFFECTIVE-IGNORES-FILEGATE
arms.find: final skipped: Null<String> = enabled && !gated && check is FileGated ? (cast check: FileGated).skipReason(file, config) : null;
arms.note: the listing ignores a rule's own per-file gate

arms.name: M-EFFECTIVE-RENDER-HEADER
arms.note: the header review tooling detects the scoped form by changes

arms.name: M-FACTS-ORACLE-AGREE
arms.note: the first of two types the configurations disagree on is answered, so an annotation is right in one build and wrong in the other

arms.name: M-FACTS-VALUE-FLOWS
arms.note: a value is typed by its own site alone, so a flow out of it at another type no longer disagrees

arms.name: M-FACTS-ORACLE-RAW-AGREE
arms.note: the first of the types the facts give a value at its range is its type, though the configurations disagree

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPELL-UNKNOWN
arms.note: an unbound monomorph is spelled Dynamic, so a type the compiler never pinned is written as one

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPELL-SCOPE
arms.note: every type parameter is in scope, so a parameter of another declaration is written where it names nothing

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPELL-IMPL
arms.note: an abstract's statics and implementation class are spelled like any path, which no source can write

arms.name: M-FACTS-ORACLE-ORIGINAL
arms.note: a rewritten file keeps no original text, so its facts cannot be placed and every declaration in it declines

arms.name: M-FACTS-INVALIDATE-FOREIGN
arms.note: facts a compile certified for the text now on disk are dropped with the rewrite, so a compile that ran after the write answers nothing

arms.name: M-FACTS-FIELD-TYPES
arms.note: a second configuration's type for a field is dropped, so a field the builds type apart reads as agreed

arms.name: M-FACTS-SIGNATURE-VARIANTS
arms.note: only the first configuration's signature is kept, so a return or parameter the builds type apart reads as agreed

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-ORACLE-PARAMS
arms.find: for (index in 0...own.length) pushEdit(out, paramOracleEdit(s, fn, own[index], index));
arms.note: the oracle-assisted pass types no parameter

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-ORACLE-FIELDS
arms.note: the oracle-assisted pass types no field

arms.name: M-EXPLICIT-TYPE-STRUCTURAL-DECLINE
arms.note: a finding the structural fix leaves unfixed says nothing about why

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-FACTS-FIRST
arms.note: the oracle-assisted phase asks the display server although the run holds every configuration's facts

arms.name: M-ASSISTED-DECLINE-CENSUS
arms.note: the oracle-assisted phase prints no decline reason

arms.name: M-FACTS-DYNAMIC-SOURCE
arms.note: a local a Dynamic value initializes is annotated with the structure its uses bound, which the value need not have

arms.name: M-BAG-INITIALIZER
arms.note: a bag declaration whose initializer is a typed structure becomes a DynamicAccess its fields may not fit

arms.name: M-BAG-NULL-OUTER
arms.note: a Null<T> value is typed by its bare wrapper, so the bag becomes DynamicAccess<Null>, which names no type

arms.name: M-JOURNAL-INTERIOR
arms.find: if (start < to && from < end) return null;

arms.name: M-OWNED-ENCLOSING-TYPE

arms.name: M-OWNED-ALIAS-IGNORED

arms.name: M-OWNED-QUALIFIED-EXPR-IGNORED

arms.name: M-OWNED-NO-SUPERTYPE-WALK

arms.name: M-INDEX-MEMO-UNVALIDATED

arms.name: M-INDEX-KEY-UNPREFIXED

arms.name: M-INDEX-MEMO-TAG-IGNORED

arms.name: M-INDEX-MEMO-OUTLIVES-AMBIENT

arms.find: if (memo != null && sameSources(memo.sources, files)) return memo.index;

arms.name: M-SKIM-GAPS-COUNTED

arms.name: M-SKIM-NEVER

arms.name: M-SKIM-BRANCH-DEPTH
arms.note: a directive branch that does not return to the depth its region opened at is balanced across branches, so a body whose branches each open a brace ends past its own close

arms.name: M-SKIM-REGION-LEFT-OPEN
arms.note: a body may end inside a directive region it opened, so the members after it are read as part of the region

arms.name: M-SKIM-OUTER-REGION

arms.name: M-SCOPE-UNPARSED-UNSPELLED

arms.name: M-TS-STORED-HOLDER-NOT-DECLARATION

arms.name: M-EXPOSED-WRAPPER-IGNORED

arms.name: M-TS-INFER-SHIFT

arms.name: M-TS-OVERLOAD-OWN-PARAMS

arms.name: M-VALUES-IMPORTED-CTOR
arms.note: an import that puts an enum in scope brings none of its constructors, so a bare pattern naming one reads as a capture

arms.name: M-VALUES-WILDCARD-CTOR
arms.note: a wildcard over an enum brings its statics only, never its constructors

arms.name: M-VALUES-ALIAS-WHOLE-MODULE
arms.note: an alias of a module's main type brings the constructors of every type of the module

arms.name: M-VALUES-FIELD-IMPORT-TYPES

arms.name: M-MACRO-VALUE-UNLISTED
arms.note: no import of a bare call name is ever out of the index's sight, so a macro an unindexed static import brings is folded into

arms.name: M-MACRO-EXTENSIONS-ONLY

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-CONSTRUCTED

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-ABSTRACT-THIS

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-PEEL

arms.name: M-OUTER-PATH-PEEL

arms.name: M-CONSTRUCTION-CTOR-GAP
arms.note: the constructor's arguments are read as the type's

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-LOCAL-INIT
arms.note: a local written with no type has none, though Haxe gives it its initializer's

arms.name: M-VOCAB-UNSET-SEAM-ADDED
arms.note: a single seam the grammar leaves unset adds an empty kind name instead of nothing

arms.name: M-GUARD-ELSE-ADMITTED
arms.note: an `if` with an `else` is inverted as if it had none, so both guard rules drop the else branch

arms.name: M-GUARD-UNBRACED-THEN
arms.note: an un-braced then-branch is taken for a block, so its braces are cut off text that has none

arms.name: M-GUARD-MIN-THEN-IGNORED
arms.note: a then-branch under the rule's minimum is inverted, so guard-return flattens a one-statement branch

arms.name: M-GUARD-GLUE-COMMENT-BLIND
arms.note: a comment in the `if (` or `) {` glue no longer refuses the rewrite, which drops it

arms.name: M-GUARD-UNCLEAN-INVERSION-REPORTED

arms.name: M-HXML-SPLIT-LAST-SPACE

arms.name: M-HXML-QUOTES-KEPT

arms.name: M-BLAMES-BASENAME

arms.name: M-COMPILEDIR-PROBE-BLIND
arms.note: the compile-dir probe reads no classpath, so every nested hxml compiles from its own directory even where its classpaths resolve from the config's

arms.name: M-GC-RUN-INHERITS
arms.note: a single haxe spawn inherits the caller's environment untouched, so every typecheck run through `run` pays the default collector again

arms.name: M-GC-DRIVER-INHERITS
arms.note: the parallel driver and every job it starts run in the caller's environment, so the overlapped typechecks run under the default collector

arms.name: M-GC-PENDING-INHERITS
arms.note: a batch started in the background (the facts compiles, the reach probes, the warm servers) runs under the default collector

arms.name: M-GC-INHERITED-OVERRIDDEN

arms.name: M-GC-OFF-IGNORED
arms.note: APQ_ORACLE_GC=off is passed to the runtime as a parameter named off instead of leaving the collector alone

arms.name: M-GC-EMPTY-DECLARED-OFF
arms.note: an empty APQ_ORACLE_GC (how a test restores an unset variable) turns the tuning off instead of meaning the default

arms.name: M-GC-MEMORY-UNCOUNTED
arms.note: the budget ignores the extra memory a tuned collector's compile holds, so a small machine runs more compiles than it has memory for

arms.name: M-DRIVER-READS-STDIN

arms.name: M-DRIVER-UNBOUNDED

arms.name: M-DRIVER-BOUND-IGNORES-ROUNDS

arms.name: M-PENDING-UNBOUNDED
arms.note: await polls a wedged background driver forever: a stopped driver still answers the liveness probe, so the run never ends

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-DO-WHILE-BODY-LAST

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-BODY-STATEMENT-BLOCK-ONLY

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-EXPR-BODY-KEPT

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-HEADER-STATEMENT-IF-ONLY
arms.note: a MERGE header must be an if-statement, so a do-while's if-expression header is never merged

arms.name: M-LOOPGUARD-BRANCH-STATEMENT-BLOCK-ONLY
arms.note: a MERGE header's branch must be a statement block, so a do-while header's block expression is never merged

arms.name: M-GUARD-CONTINUE-DEFERS-STATEMENT-BLOCK-ONLY

arms.name: M-BINDER-NAMED-FN-NO-STEP-OUT

arms.name: M-VOCAB-NESTED-NO-NAMED-FN

arms.name: M-REMOVE-ELEMENT-KIND-IGNORED

arms.name: M-REWRITE-NAME-CAPTURE-HOLE

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-IGNORED

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-STATIC-LOST

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-COPIES-ASSIGNED

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-WRITTEN-TYPE-TRUSTED

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-TYPE-PARAMS-BLIND

arms.name: M-COND-NAMED-FN-NOT-IN-EFFECT

arms.name: M-COND-CONTINUATION-NOT-IN-EFFECT

arms.name: M-SITES-EXPR-RETURN-NO-LANDING

arms.name: M-VOCAB-DOWHILE-EXPR-NOT-LOOP

arms.name: M-RLW-NAMED-FN-NOT-BINDER

arms.name: M-RLW-LOCAL-FN-AS-BINDER

arms.name: M-DOWHILE-PLAIN-SEMI

arms.name: M-NAMED-FN-STMT-NO-ARM

arms.name: M-NAMED-FN-NOT-BRACE-ENDED

arms.name: M-NAMED-FN-EXPR-BODY-RELAXED
arms.note: a named literal's EXPRESSION body ends its statement with no `;`, so `x = function n() return 1 trace(x());` (Haxe: `Missing ;`) parses

arms.name: M-VOCAB-WHILE-EXPR-NOT-BRANCH

arms.name: M-WALK-TYPE-ARGS-UNCOUNTED

arms.name: M-CONDBRANCH-TYPE-ARGS-DROPPED

arms.name: M-VALUES-MODULE-WITHIN

arms.name: M-VALUES-MODULE-ALTERNATIVE

arms.name: M-KEEP-BARE-IGNORED

arms.name: M-KEEP-BARE-CLASH-BLIND

arms.name: M-KEEP-BARE-NOT-MAIN

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-GUARDED-MEMBER

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-NOUSING

arms.name: M-NAMING-ENUMVALUE-PROPERTY

arms.name: M-NAMING-ENUMVALUE-STATIC

arms.name: M-NAMING-OUTSIDE-SCOPE-IGNORED

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-ON

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-NO-RETURN

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-NO-BLOCK
arms.note: a braced else branch `{ return false; }` is not read through, so it is inverted while the bare one is kept

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-NO-PAREN

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-ANY-LITERAL
arms.note: every else arm counts as a default, so `!a ? x : 1` is no longer inverted under the option

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-KEEP-DEFAULT-THEN-ARM
arms.note: a ternary builder asks the gate about the THEN value: `if (!a) y = x; else y = 0;` is oriented positive to `y = a ? 0 : x;` under the option

arms.name: M-PTR-KEEP-DEFAULT-THEN-ARM

arms.name: M-INVERT-KEEP-DEFAULT-STATEMENT-THEN-ARM

arms.name: M-INVERT-KEEP-DEFAULT-VALUE-THEN-ARM

arms.name: M-DEFLIT-FALSE-DROPPED

arms.name: M-DEFLIT-EMPTY-STRING-DROPPED

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-ANY-COND

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-BOTH-LITERALS

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-RETURN-MISMATCH

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-BOOL-COND

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-ON
arms.note: `defaultLast` is read as on when no config sets it, so every project silently turns `a ? null : x`

arms.name: M-NEGCOND-DEFAULT-LAST-NO-KEEP

arms.name: M-INVERT-DEFAULT-LAST-STATEMENT-MESSAGE

arms.name: M-ARM-LEDGER-HANDOFF-KEPT
arms.note: the safe arm's hand-off declines stay beside the arm's own verdict, so each arm finding is declined twice, or declined although the arm fixed it

arms.name: M-ARM-LEDGER-HANDOFF-UNRECORDED
arms.note: no hand-off is recorded, so the risky phase has nothing to take back and the arm findings are declined twice

arms.name: M-ARM-LEDGER-ARM-BLIND
arms.note: the safe loop does not ask the RiskyArm which findings its arm owns, so no hand-off is ever recorded

arms.name: M-LEDGER-ARM-LISTED-ABSENT
arms.note: a RiskyArm rule is footnoted as absent from the ledger (and counted never asked) beside its own row

arms.name: M-RETAIN-SOURCES-KEEPS-ALL
arms.note: nothing is ever dropped, so a --fix run keeps every superseded and speculative parse for the rest of the run (the N25 self-fix OOM at the default heap)

arms.name: M-RETAIN-SOURCES-DROPS-LIVE
arms.find: final keep: Map<String, Bool> = [for (source in live) source => true];
arms.note: the live sources are dropped too, so every pass re-parses every file and an unchanged file loses its tree identity across passes

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-OFF
arms.note: no trial is moved: every enum-branch trial stays inline in its rule and BranchOutliningTest reads the unchanged body

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-WRITE-BLIND
arms.find: refuse('a write to the rule local $name');
arms.note: a trial that writes a rule local is moved, so the helper writes its own copy and the rule never sees the write

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-BREAK-BLIND
arms.find: if (_loops == 0) refuse('a break / continue that leaves the trial');
arms.note: a break that leaves the trial is moved into a helper, where it has no loop to target

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-SWITCH-BLIND
arms.note: a trial holding a switch is moved although its pattern bindings are not scoped

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-FOR-PATTERN-BLIND
arms.find: refuse('a for over a non-identifier pattern');
arms.note: a for over a key-value pattern is moved although its bindings are not scoped

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-NULLABLE-RETURN-BLIND
arms.find: if (_fns == 0 && !cannotBeNull(value)) refuse('a return whose value may be null');
arms.note: a return that may hand back null is moved, and the call site reads that null as a failed trial and tries the next branch

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-CONSTANT-AS-CTOR
arms.note: an all-capitals constant counts as a constructor, so its possibly-null value is returned through a helper

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-UNTYPED-CAPTURE
arms.note: a captured rule local with no single declared type becomes a helper parameter without a type

arms.name: M-OUTLINE-NESTED-ALT-BLIND
arms.note: the outer trial of a moved nested trial returns _alt and stays inline

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-FROZEN-STALE
arms.find: if (last != null && lastFacts != null && sameReadState(last, state)) return lastFacts;
arms.replace: if (last != null && lastFacts != null) return lastFacts;
arms.note: a recording walk hands every visit the facts it froze first, so the replay answers what the state held at the first visit of the unit

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-MEMO-SEED-BLIND
arms.find: if (cache == null || seed != null || declaredNullable != null || typeSources != null) {
arms.replace: if (cache == null || declaredNullable != null || typeSources != null) {
arms.note: a seeded walk is answered from the seedless recording and loses every MaybeNull the seed makes

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-MEMO-DECLARED-BLIND
arms.find: if (cache == null || seed != null || declaredNullable != null || typeSources != null) {
arms.replace: if (cache == null || seed != null || typeSources != null) {
arms.note: a declaredNullable walk is answered from the seedless recording and loses the annotation seed

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-MEMO-TYPES-BLIND
arms.find: if (cache == null || seed != null || declaredNullable != null || typeSources != null) {
arms.replace: if (cache == null || seed != null || declaredNullable != null) {
arms.note: a walk given the written types is answered from the recording made without them, so a non-null predicate call no longer narrows

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-MEMO-SOURCE-BLIND
arms.find: if (known != null) return known.source == source ? known.visits : record();
arms.note: a tree asked about with another source is answered from the recording made over the first

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-MEMO-NOT-FORGOTTEN
arms.note: forget keeps the recording, so a pass that re-reads a superseded tree replays it and the memory N36 releases stays held

arms.name: M-SAMEITEMS-LENGTH-ONLY
arms.find: for (i => item in a) if (item != b[i]) return false;
arms.note: two arrays of one length count as the same whatever they hold

arms.name: M-SORTED-OFFSETS-LOWER-BLIND
arms.note: the search never moves past an offset below the range, so the first offset of the array answers

arms.name: M-SORTED-OFFSETS-UPPER-BLIND
arms.find: return lo < sorted.length && sorted[lo] < to ? sorted[lo] : -1;
arms.note: an offset at or past the upper bound answers, so ArgumentValues reads the written type of the NEXT declaration

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-COMPOUND
arms.note: a compound assignment of a constant (`threw += 1;`) counts as recording an outcome, though it reads the local it writes

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-VALUE
arms.note: any value counts as a recorded outcome, so `threw = compute();` and `threw = other;` hide a handler that runs code

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-DECL-KIND
arms.note: a parameter of the enclosing function counts as an outcome local

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-FN-BOUND
arms.note: a read after the CLOSURE the try sits in counts as reading the outcome, though the closure runs whenever it is called

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-EVERY-STMT
arms.find: if (hit == null || !readAfter(hit, tree, ancestors, fnAt, scan)) return false;
arms.replace:
if (hit == null || !readAfter(hit, tree, ancestors, fnAt, scan)) return false;
		break;
arms.note: only the FIRST statement of the body is checked, so a call or an unread second local after it rides along

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-READ-KIND
arms.note: a WRITE of the local after the try counts as reading the outcome

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-READ-BINDING
arms.note: a read of the same NAME bound to another declaration counts as reading the outcome

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-READ-AFTER
arms.note: a read BEFORE the try counts as reading the outcome after it

arms.name: M-SWALLOW-OUTCOME-STMT-LIST
arms.note: a read in the other arm of the branch the try sits in counts, though it follows the try in the text and on no path

arms.name: M-NAMING-PROPERTY-MODS-NONE
arms.note: no property earns a storage modifier, so a storage-less private property needs the `_` again and a static read-only one is a camelCase public field

arms.name: M-NAMING-STORAGELESS-ISVAR
arms.note: an `@:isVar` property counts as storage-less, so its storage escapes the private-field rule

arms.name: M-NAMING-STORAGELESS-REGION
arms.note: a run that steps over a `#if` region counts as proven, so an `@:isVar` one build sees there is missed

arms.name: M-ACCESSOR-STORAGELESS-TRUE
arms.note: every accessor clause counts as storage-less, so a `null` / `default` slot leaves the field rules too

arms.name: M-NAMING-STORAGELESS-RULE-PUBLIC
arms.note: the storage-less property rule reaches a PUBLIC property, whose `_` the public-field rule rejects

arms.name: M-NAMING-READONLY-IGNORES-WRITE
arms.note: a `(get, set)` property reads as read-only, so a public static one takes the constant format

arms.name: M-NAMING-READONLY-RULE-INSTANCE
arms.note: an INSTANCE read-only property takes the static-final format too

arms.name: M-TS-EXH-WRITES-ANY
arms.note: every write of the member's name counts, whatever object it may reach

arms.name: M-HELPER-THIS-KEPT
arms.find: edits.movedTextEdits.push({ span: hit.span, text: hit.interpolated ? '$$${edits.param}' : edits.param });
arms.note: a bare `this` in a moved body is left standing, so the static helper reads a `this` it does not have

arms.name: M-HELPER-MEMBER-UNQUALIFIED
arms.note: a moved body's bare read of a member staying on the source is left bare instead of `<param>.x` / `Src.x`

arms.name: M-HELPER-NO-GRANT
arms.note: a moved body reading a private member of the source gets no `@:access` grant

arms.name: M-HELPER-FIELDS-TRAVEL
arms.note: the fields only the moved methods touch move into the static helper as instance fields, although the methods read them through their parameter

arms.name: M-HELPER-CONSTANT-STAYS
arms.note: a private constant only the moved members read stays behind on the source

arms.name: M-HELPER-TYPE-STAYS
arms.note: a private type only the moved code names stays in the source module, where the helper module cannot see it

arms.name: M-HELPER-TRAVELLING-IMPORTED
arms.find: final travels: Bool = travelling != null && travelling.contains(ref.name);
arms.note: a type travelling with the move is still priced as a dependency to import, and the carry refuses it as unreachable

arms.name: M-HELPER-CALL-ORDER
arms.note: call rewrites inserting at one offset are pushed outermost first, so `a.self().add(1)` comes out with its heads swapped

arms.name: M-HELPER-SUBTYPE-CALLERS-SKIPPED
arms.find: final subtypeError: Null<String> = subtypeBareCallers(edits, indexes, calls);
arms.note: a subtype's bare call of an inherited moved member is left calling a member its supertype no longer declares

arms.name: M-HELPER-ARM-RETARGET-NONE
arms.note: an arm addressing a moved member is not reported for retargeting

arms.name: M-HELPER-ARM-STALE-NONE
arms.note: an arm whose find the rewrite changed is not flagged

arms.name: M-HELPER-ACCESSOR-ALLOWED
arms.note: a property accessor moves into the helper, where `<param>.p` calls the accessor it used to implement

arms.name: M-HELPER-FIELD-ALLOWED
arms.note: an instance field is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-HELPER-MODIFIER-ALLOWED
arms.note: a `dynamic` / `macro` member moves into a static helper, which keeps neither meaning

arms.name: M-HELPER-VALUE-USE-ALLOWED
arms.find: if (placed == null || open < 0) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, m.name, where(file, source, offset));
arms.replace: if (placed == null) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, m.name, where(file, source, offset));
arms.note: a moved member passed as a function value is rewritten as though it were called

arms.name: M-HELPER-SUPER-ALLOWED
arms.note: a `super` access is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-HELPER-UNRESOLVED-ALLOWED
arms.note: a name nothing in scope binds is left as it is, though it may be a member of a supertype the index cannot see

arms.name: M-HELPER-SHARED-TYPE-ALLOWED
arms.note: a private type the staying code names too is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-HELPER-PARAM-CLASH-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a parameter name the moved code already spells is taken, and the local shadows it

arms.name: M-HELPER-GENERIC-ALLOWED
arms.note: a generic source moves with a parameter type missing its type parameters

arms.name: M-HELPER-NON-CLASS-ALLOWED
arms.note: an abstract's member moves into a helper, where `this` is no longer its underlying value

arms.name: M-HELPER-DRY-RUN-WRITES
arms.note: a dry run writes the files it was only asked to print

arms.name: M-HELPER-RECEIVER-VALUE-ALLOWED
arms.find: if (open < 0) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, h.m.name, where(h.file, source, h.at));
arms.replace: if (false) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, h.m.name, where(h.file, source, h.at));
arms.note: a moved member reached through a receiver as a function value (`this.f.bind(1)`) is rewritten as though it were called

arms.name: M-HELPER-MODULE-VALUE-ALLOWED
arms.note: a module-level value of the source module is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-WRITE-DIR-UNCREATED
arms.note: a write into a missing directory no longer creates it

arms.name: M-WRITE-DIR-KEPT
arms.note: a change set that is not written keeps the directories it created

arms.name: M-USING-MEMBER-FIRST-OFF
arms.note: a `.method` access the `using` provably takes no part in counts as an extension use again

arms.name: M-UNUSED-USING-NO-DOOR
arms.note: unused-import stops asking the door

arms.name: M-CARRY-USING-DOOR-OFFSET
arms.note: the carry asks the door at declaration-relative offsets

arms.name: M-MEMBER-BINDS-STATIC
arms.note: a static of the name reads as shadowing the extension

arms.name: M-MEMBER-BINDS-GUARDED
arms.note: a member under `#if` reads as binding in every build

arms.name: M-MEMBER-BINDS-HOST-GUARDED
arms.note: a declaring type under `#if` reads as declaring the member in every build

arms.name: M-STD-MEMBER-STATIC
arms.note: a static std member reads as an instance one

arms.name: M-STD-MEMBER-VIA-GUARD
arms.note: a std member reached through a guarded typedef reads as unguarded

arms.name: M-STD-MEMBER-ANY-CANDIDATE
arms.note: one std module of a simple name proving the member is enough

arms.name: M-MEMBER-DOOR-SHADOW
arms.note: the std listing answers for a name a project type takes

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-DECL-TYPE-DROPPED
arms.note: a moved declaration initializer loses its declared type, so a constant whose value is no bare literal reaches the destination untyped

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ALWAYS-BARE
arms.note: the source never gains the import, so a reference from another package names a type it cannot see

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-WILDCARD-IGNORED
arms.note: a same-package reference relies on the bare name although a wildcard import of the source may shadow it

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-NEVER-INLINE
arms.note: a scalar literal moves into a plain static final, so a parameter default it replaces no longer folds

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ALWAYS-INLINE
arms.note: every constant expression is made inline, beyond what inline-constant proves the compiler folds

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ALWAYS-PUBLIC
arms.note: a constant the enclosing type keeps for itself is exported

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-SHARED-IGNORED
arms.note: an array literal moves into one shared static instance without the caller asserting that no reader mutates it

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ANY-AGGREGATE
arms.note: an array literal holding a non-constant element moves as a constant

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-READS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an expression reading a local is refused only as a non-constant, without the name it reads

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-META-POSITION
arms.note: a metadata argument becomes a constant reference, where the metadata needs a literal

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-CASE-PATTERN
arms.note: a case pattern literal becomes a reference, which the match reads as a capture or a constant of another kind

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-PARAM-DEFAULT
arms.note: a parameter default is replaced by a constant that does not fold

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-SHADOW-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a local named like the receiving type takes the new reference

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-REBIND-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an import or type of the source that binds the receiving type name takes the new reference

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ANY-HOST
arms.note: an interface or other non-class type is handed a static final

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-UNSEEN-TYPE
arms.find: final unseen: Null<String> = request.dest == null ? null : firstUnseenType(declType, plugin);
arms.note: a declared project type travels into a module that may not see it

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-CONSTANT-ADDRESSED-UNROUTED
arms.note: the addressed flags reach the literal modes, which reject them

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-DOC-STAYS
arms.find: final from: Int = ElementSpan.docExtendedSpan(source, spanOf(moved[0]), regions, true).from;
arms.note: the slice leaves its first element's doc behind, where it documents the next element

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-RANGE-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a range past the array moves a shorter slice than asked, or none

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-READS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an element reading a local moves where that local does not exist

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-UNSEEN-TYPE
arms.find: final unseen: Null<String> = crossModule ? ExtractConstantTo.firstUnseenType(element, plugin) : null;
arms.note: an element naming a project type moves into a module that may not see it

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-NESTS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a slice is moved into its own array

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-TARGET-POSITION
arms.note: a target position is resolved after the cut, where it points at other code

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-SOURCE-UNVERIFIED
arms.note: a source that did not lose exactly the slice passes the check

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-ORDER-UNVERIFIED
arms.note: an append that lost the slice order passes the check as a multiset

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-DRY-RUN-UNROUTED
arms.note: --dry-run prints the two previews instead of the entries and their digest

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-ARG
arms.note: a spawns object entry's main positions run on a worker like every other argument

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-CONTEXT
arms.note: a value at a main position takes the spawn's background context

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-REPEAT
arms.note: a value run on the main thread at a main position is not one marshalled per post: a worker loop posting it runs as once

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-SHIFT
arms.find: return index < own && !mayShift(g, id, index, count);
arms.note: an argument a skipped optional may shift onto a later parameter is taken at its written position

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-SIGNATURE
arms.note: a call two signatures may answer is taken to bind each argument at its position

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-ARG-POSITION
arms.find: { index: i - first, count: args.length - first }
arms.note: an argument position counts the callee child too

arms.name: M-TS-OPT-SPAWN-OBJECT
arms.find: problems.push('$SPAWNS_KEY[$i] "$named": ${wrong.join(', ')} — kept as a plain entry');
arms.note: a malformed spawns object entry is kept as a plain one without a word

arms.name: M-TS-REGISTER-MEMBER
arms.note: a registers entry naming a project member is ignored for repetition, as a bare name is

arms.name: M-JSON-ROOT-UNTIGHTENED
arms.note: the root value keeps the span the parser gives it, which starts at offset 0 over the document's leading whitespace, so the writer finds no delimiter at the root's first byte

arms.name: M-JSON-DIRTY-NEVER
arms.note: no gap counts as touched by an edit, so an appended entry keeps the raw ` ` after its `,` and a deletion leaves the doubled space it closed up

arms.name: M-JSON-TOUCH-IGNORED
arms.find: || ((mark.from == mark.to || gap.from == gap.to) && mark.from <= gap.to && gap.from <= mark.to)
arms.note: only an OVERLAPPING mark touches a gap: the empty gaps around the first entry of an empty container are never re-derived, so it stays `["x"]` under an expanded parent

arms.name: M-JSON-NOTHING-NEW
arms.note: no node counts as introduced by an edit, so a new object is written as an existing one with every gap touched — inline, whatever its sibling's shape

arms.name: M-JSON-STYLE-ALWAYS-EXPANDED
arms.note: every touched container is laid out one entry per line, so an entry appended to an inline array breaks it open

arms.name: M-JSON-EMPTY-INLINE
arms.note: a container with no untouched gap is inline instead of following its parent, so the first entry of an empty array under an expanded object stays on the array's line

arms.name: M-JSON-NEW-MODEL-IGNORED
arms.find: final shaped: Null<QueryNode> = model != null && model.kind == node.kind && model.children.length > 0 ? model : null;
arms.note: a new container never looks at its nearest sibling, so a new object beside an inline one comes out expanded

arms.name: M-JSON-KEYSEP-DEFAULT
arms.note: a new member's `:` always takes the default spacing, so a document written `"a" : 1` gains a `"b": 2`

arms.name: M-JSON-INDENT-DEFAULT
arms.note: the indent unit is always a tab, so a line an edit adds to a two-space document is indented by a tab

arms.name: M-JSON-LINE-END-LF
arms.note: every line an edit adds ends in LF, so a CRLF document gains mixed line ends

arms.name: M-JSON-MARKS-UNSHIFTED
arms.note: each edit's footprint is placed at its offset in the ORIGINAL document, so a second insert's mark misses the entry it introduced

arms.name: M-QUERY-NAME-IGNORED
arms.note: a `@:queryName` field names nothing, so a JSON object member projects unnamed and `Member:<key>` matches no node

arms.name: M-LAYOUT-SPLICE-BYPASSED
arms.note: a format-preserving grammar's edits are spliced raw, so an entry appended to a one-per-line JSON array lands as `, x` on the previous line

arms.name: M-PICK-PLUGIN-FOR-IGNORES-PATH
arms.note: the file's extension is ignored, so the `--lang haxe` the shim prepends parses a `.json` file as Haxe and every JSON edit is refused

arms.name: M-COMMA-CONTAINER-KINDS-UNREAD
arms.note: a sole entry has no adjacent `,`, and the container kind is no longer asked, so an insert after it is joined by a newline instead of a `,` and the result does not parse

arms.name: M-JSON-LITERAL-NONE
arms.note: no JSON string reads as a literal, so `--sorted` refuses every JSON array as holding no constant strings

arms.name: M-JSON-REGIONS-NONE
arms.note: the JSON grammar reports no string region, so every byte of a key or a string value reads as code

arms.name: M-JSON-PATTERN-NO-METAVAR
arms.note: a `"$x"` string in a pattern stays a string, so a JSON pattern can hold no metavariable

arms.name: M-PAREN-BROKEN-CHAIN-PINNED
arms.note: an expression paren around a `+`/`-` chain an operand already broke pins that chain flat again when no `expressionWrapping` rule is set, so every continuation line renders at column 0 and the next write re-indents it

arms.name: M-BREAK-MULTI-ITEM-HOST-OFF
arms.find: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : open != '{';
arms.replace: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : false;
arms.note: a list of several items stops following a break nested in one of them, so a call around `bar(b, [for …])` stays glued while the literal breaks under it and the next write opens it one argument per line

arms.name: M-BREAK-OBJECT-LITERAL-HOST
arms.find: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : open != '{';
arms.replace: final offered: Bool = items.length == 1 ? flatSingle : true;
arms.note: an object literal's field list is wrapped in alternatives too, which hides the literal's width decision from its Allman placement: a comprehension body carrying a comprehension in a field breaks glued and goes Allman one write late

arms.name: M-BREAK-EVERY-NODE
arms.note: every node of a break is offered again by every list it is nested in, so the alternatives, and the Doc, grow exponentially with the nesting depth

arms.name: M-BREAK-COMMITTED-BARE
arms.note: a literal broken by its own width is laid out bare where the next write reads it in a `BodyGroup` every width probe defers, so a method chain dot-breaks and an arrow body leaves `->` on the first write and both glue back on the second

arms.name: M-PAREN-MEASURES-COMMITTED
arms.note: an expression paren measures a committed literal break deferred, so the paren that opens for every narrower literal glues once the literal breaks: one write still, but onto the other fixed point than the one the paren reached before

arms.name: M-BREAK-READBACK-BARE
arms.note: a literal its own rule breaks statically keeps the bare layout where the next write reads it back in a `BodyGroup`, so an arrow body it leads leaves `->` on the first write and glues back on the second

arms.name: M-OWNED-TIER-NO-USE-SITE
arms.note: a simple name is resolved with no use site, so a #if-guarded import never decides a use inside its own branch and the receiver reads as unknown

arms.name: M-OWNED-MEMO-IGNORES-SITE
arms.note: a file holding a guarded import answers every use of a name as its first use did, whichever #if branch each sits in

arms.name: M-OWNED-CANDIDATES-IGNORED
arms.note: an Unknown name whose every candidate is read and none is owned is still reported, by the member name alone

arms.name: M-OWNED-OUTSIDE-CANDIDATE-IGNORED
arms.note: a candidate outside the index — a std type a guarded alias names — is never the owned type

arms.name: M-BINDING-EITHER-DROPS-REST
arms.note: a guarded statement's candidates leave out what the builds without it bind

arms.name: M-BINDING-EITHER-DROPS-GUARDED
arms.note: a guarded statement's candidates leave out what the statement itself binds

arms.name: M-BINDING-EITHER-OPEN-READ
arms.find: mine == null || theirs == null ? Unreadable(null) : Either(mine.concat(theirs))
arms.note: the other builds' binding nothing reads is dropped from the candidates instead of leaving them open

arms.name: M-BINDING-CANDIDATES-OWN-TYPE
arms.note: a name the module declares itself is given the candidates its imports bind, although its own type outranks them

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-LOCAL-CONSTRUCTION
arms.note: a local written with no type and initialised by a construction stays untyped

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-INITIALIZER-ONE-STEP
arms.note: a local initialised by another local that holds a construction stays untyped

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-SAME-ARGS
arms.note: a duplicate is judged by the entry NAME again, so a second `@:access(...)` with another argument is refused although Haxe allows several

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-ENTRY-NEVER-SAME
arms.note: no entry ever equals the one being added, so the exact repeat of an annotation is added a second time

arms.name: M-ADDIMPORT-CLI-BLIND-SEAT
arms.note: the op reads the file with no project resolution scope, so the insert seat takes every wildcard for a run boundary and places the import where the import-order rule does not

arms.name: M-SLOTS-FIT-SKIPS
arms.find: if (p.optional && !p.rest && fit != Fits) step(walk, arg, param + 1);
arms.note: an argument that fits an optional parameter may also skip it, so `f(?a:Int, ?b:String, c:Int)` called `f(1)` reads as binding `c`

arms.name: M-SLOTS-MISFIT-BINDS
arms.note: an argument binds a parameter it misfits, so `g(true)` keeps `true` in `?a:Int` as well

arms.name: M-SLOTS-MAYFIT-BINDS-ONLY
arms.note: an undecided fit only binds, so the way the compiler skips the parameter is lost

arms.name: M-SLOTS-MANDATORY-MISFIT
arms.note: a mandatory parameter an argument misfits is skipped, so a call that cannot compile reads as binding the next one

arms.name: M-SLOTS-UNBOUND-MANDATORY
arms.find: for (p in param ... params.length) if (!params[p].optional && !params[p].rest) return;

arms.name: M-TYPING-KEY-OFFSET

arms.name: M-TYPING-TYPE-KEY-FILE

arms.name: M-BREAKMARK-REBUILD-FRESH-TOKEN

arms.name: M-TS-LAMBDA-SITE-UNGUARDED

arms.name: M-TS-BIND-MEMO-ONE-VALUATION

arms.name: M-TS-SITE-MEMO-BY-CALLER

arms.name: M-CG-DISPATCH-MEMO-LEAKS
arms.note: the dispatch memo outlives the edges it was kept for: a query after a file is taken out answers the overrides read before

arms.name: M-CG-DISPATCH-MEMO-BY-TYPE
arms.note: the dispatch memo keys by the receiver type alone: the first member dispatched on a type answers for every other

arms.name: M-DROPPED-SEP-UNREHOMED
arms.note: a list whose trailing separator the writer drops is laid out from the source tree, the comment outside the element the next parse reads it inside of

arms.name: M-DROPPED-SEP-KEPT-REHOMED

arms.name: M-DROPPED-SEP-BLOCK-REHOMED

arms.name: M-TAIL-SLOT-OVERWRITTEN

arms.name: M-TAIL-ALT-SLOT-OVERWRITTEN
arms.note: a ctor close slot already holding a comment is overwritten, and that comment is lost

arms.name: M-TAIL-WRITTEN-SEMICOLON-IGNORED

arms.name: M-TAIL-ONLY-KNOWN-METAS
arms.note: a shape with a token after its operand (a paren pair, a trail literal) passes the comment into the operand, ahead of that token

arms.name: M-TAIL-ABSENT-FIELD-STOPS
arms.note: an absent optional last field (an if with no else) answers null instead of the field emitted before it

arms.name: M-TAIL-ARRAY-SLOT-UNREAD
arms.note: an array literal tail no longer takes the comment its close captures

arms.name: M-TAIL-CALL-SLOT-UNREAD
arms.note: a call tail no longer takes the comment its close paren captures

arms.name: M-REGION-UNNAMED

arms.name: M-REGION-MARK-ALWAYS

arms.name: M-REGION-OFFER-THROUGH-BODIES

arms.name: M-NESTED-THROUGH-BODIES

arms.name: M-REGION-SEAMS-BOUNDED

arms.name: M-UNIFY-ALIAS-STOP

arms.name: M-STRUCT-READONLY-INVARIANT

arms.name: M-STRUCT-MUTABLE-SAME-DECL

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-SELF-PARAMS

arms.name: M-ADDIMPORT-USING-TAKES-IMPORT-SEAT

arms.name: M-ADDIMPORT-PATH-UNCHECKED

arms.name: M-REMOVEIMPORT-KEYWORD-IGNORED

arms.name: M-REMOVEIMPORT-CLI-USING-FLAG-DROPPED

arms.name: M-LIT-QUALIFIED-KINDS-IGNORED

arms.name: M-HOIST-USINGS-SOURCE-ORDER

arms.name: M-TCO-KNOB-IGNORED

arms.name: M-TCO-LEADING-IGNORED

arms.name: M-TCO-DIRECTIVE-MOVED

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-TAB-ROW

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-CODE-SHAPED

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-SPLITS-CODE-SPAN

arms.name: M-COMMENT-DIRECTIVE-NONE

arms.name: M-LITERAL-WRAPPER-SKIPPED

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-NO-EDIT

arms.name: M-ASYM-FIX-UNTERMINATED

arms.name: M-INDEX-RETURN-SOURCE-SPAN
arms.replace: returnSource: seams.functionKinds.contains(child.kind) ? maps.returnTypeSources[typeKey]?.trim() ?? [for (bounds in maps.typeParamConstraints[typeKey] ?? []) for (b in bounds) b].pop() : null,
