arms.name: M-CALLS-NULLABLE-UNBOUND
arms.note: an argument of a `Null<…>` type binds a type parameter to the type inside, so `id(n)` over `?n:Int` is an `Int`

arms.name: M-CASTS-APPLIED-WRITTEN
arms.find: r == null ? Open : appliedEnd(r, [for (a in written) endIn(a, file, at, params)]);
arms.note: a generic abstract written with type arguments stands for no end, so `m(true)` over `E2<String, Float>` leaves both candidates open

arms.name: M-CASTS-APPLIED-ALIAS
arms.note: a typedef aliasing a generic abstract with type arguments stands for the bare abstract, so `k(true)` over `Path` leaves both candidates open

arms.name: M-CASTS-APPLIED-GRAPH-PARAM
arms.note: a clause written as a type parameter is not read as its argument, so an applied abstract takes nothing through `from A`

arms.name: M-CASTS-APPLIED-SAME
arms.note: an applied abstract is not itself applied alike, so `Box<String>` misfits `Box<String>`

arms.name: M-GRAPH-RETURN-BOUND
arms.replace: g._facts.returnSources, id, CallGraphNames.returnSourceOf(node, returnSources) ?? [for (b in bounds[span.from] ?? []) for (t in b) t].pop(), first
arms.note: a function written with no return type reads a type parameter's bound beside it as its return, so `g(f).run()` runs the bound's `run`

arms.name: M-BINDER-RETURN-ANNOTATION
arms.replace: final written: Null<String> = [for (c in fn.children) if ((_shape.typeAnnotationKinds ?? []).contains(c.kind)) _source.substring(c.span?.from ?? 0, c.span?.to ?? 0)].pop();
arms.note: a function's result is its last annotation child, so a type parameter's bound beside no return type types the lambda it returns

arms.name: M-BINDER-LOCAL-CALL-ANNOTATION
arms.note: a local function's result is its last annotation child, so a call of one written with no return type is its type parameter's bound

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-RECEIVER-INHERITED
arms.find: if (hit != null) for (m in hit.members) out.push({ type: hit.host.type, member: m, file: hit.host.file });
arms.note: a namesake inheriting the member is left out, so the one declaring it answers for a receiver of either: `s.write('a')` is the namesake's `Void`

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-RECEIVER-DECLARATIONS
arms.note: the name walk reads only the namesakes declaring the member, so `s.write('a')` is the namesake's `Void`

arms.name: M-SOURCE-RECEIVER-DECLARATIONS
arms.note: the source currency reads only the namesakes declaring the member, so `s.write('a')` is the namesake's `Void`

arms.name: M-BUILDS-ONE-BRANCH
arms.note: a declaration written once asks the builds too, so a run probes its builds for a question no build can change

arms.name: M-BUILDS-NONE-KNOWN
arms.find: if (liveness == null || source == null) return all;
arms.note: with no build known no branch is read, so a declaration one branch of which is a `typedef` types its value

arms.name: M-BUILDS-FILTER-OFF
arms.find: final kept: Array<DeclBranch> = all.filter(b -> liveness.live(file, source, b.span));
arms.note: a branch every declared build leaves out is still read, so a `typedef` branch to a target type keeps the value untyped

arms.name: M-BUILDS-NONE-LIVE
arms.note: a declaration no build compiles reads as one with no branch, so every branch vacuously declares any value

arms.name: M-BUILDS-ASKED-ONCE
arms.note: the builds are read again for every question about a declaration with several branches

arms.name: M-BUILDS-HOST-OFF
arms.find: final read: () -> Null<ReachBuilds> = host == null ? () -> null : host.reachBuilds;
arms.note: the run's builds are never read, so every branch stays read under builds that leave one out

arms.name: M-CASTS-CLAUSES-NULL
arms.note: a branch that is no abstract is passed over, so a `typedef` branch no longer keeps the declaration unmodelled

arms.name: M-CASTS-CLAUSES-LIVE
arms.note: the clauses of every branch are read, a dead `typedef` branch's included, so the cast graph is lost under the builds

arms.name: M-CASTS-BRANCHES-LIVE
arms.find: return clausesOf(r) == null ? null : [for (b in _builds.of(r)) membersOf(r, b)];
arms.replace: return clausesOf(r) == null ? null : [for (b in r.type.branches) membersOf(r, b)];
arms.note: a dead branch's members count as one build's, so the value its `typedef` branch lacks is no value

arms.name: M-CASTS-MEMBERS-LIVE
arms.find: final members: Array<MemberInfo> = [for (b in _builds.of(r)) for (m in membersOf(r, b)) m];
arms.note: a conversion member only a dead branch declares converts, so `V` takes a `String` no build lets it take

arms.name: M-INDEX-BRANCHES-ALTERNATE
arms.note: the alternate branch's record is lost, so a declaration whose `#else` is a `typedef` reads as one abstract

arms.name: M-PAREN-KEPT-CHAIN-OPENS
arms.note: a `keep` chain its source broke opens the paren its source glued again, adding a break after `(` and before `)` the source does not have

arms.name: M-PAREN-KEPT-CHAIN-SOURCE-NEST
arms.note: the glued paren nests its kept chain by the SOURCE break after `return`, which the `return` policy may drop or add, so one write is no longer a fixed point

arms.name: M-CATCH-BLOCK-LINE-END-GLUED
arms.note: a block comment that ended its source line after the try body's `}` glues the first `catch` onto its line again under a same-line policy

arms.name: M-PAREN-KEPT-CHAIN-OPERAND
arms.note: a kept chain broken only inside an operand (an array one item per line) counts as one its source broke, so its paren stays glued instead of opening

arms.name: M-THRESHOLD-ARG-UNNAMED
arms.note: an object-literal argument deciding its own threshold break is no longer named, so the argument list lays itself out from the flat literal and the next write, reading the broken literal back committed, packs the list differently

arms.name: M-SIBLING-OFFER-UNALIASED
arms.note: the emitted widest case unit no longer ties its named break to the sibling offer, so the measure render never takes the offer and the switch spreads on the flat width the next write no longer reads

arms.name: M-NAMED-FIT-PIVOT
arms.note: an object-literal argument under a FIT cascade is named too, though the next write re-decides it instead of reading it back committed, so a call the source opened one argument per line is rewritten into a hug

arms.name: M-CHAIN-OFFER-OFF
arms.note: a binary chain or ternary no longer re-lays itself out for an operand whose nested break commits, so a ternary hugs a call whose literal broke and the next write, reading that literal back with a hardline, breaks the ternary

arms.name: M-OFFER-COPIES-WHOLE
arms.note: a rewrite copies every node it walks instead of sharing what it leaves unchanged, so each offered alternative copies its host whole and nested hosts grow the Doc exponentially in depth

arms.name: M-OFFER-REPLACES-BOTH-SIDES
arms.find: f == flat ? n : BreakCommit(brk, f, token);
arms.replace: f == flat ? n : BreakCommit(walk(brk), f, token);
arms.note: an offer also rewrites the other breaks' alternatives it passes, so every nested host re-walks and re-copies all of them and a deep paren chain writes in a high power of its depth

arms.name: M-OFFER-REPLACED-COPIES
arms.note: an offer copies every node it walks again, both sides of every other break included, so each nested host copies the alternatives below it whole and the build grows exponentially with the nesting depth

arms.name: M-IMPORT-MODULE-TAIL-UNKNOWN
arms.note: a path past its module binds a known set only when the index declares that very type, so a static-field import or one of a type a build macro makes reads as an unknown set, counts as a second binder of every statement, and refuses every hoist in a directory where one module imports a function

arms.name: M-HOIST-RECEIVER-UNVOUCHED
arms.note: every governed module is taken to resolve a statement it would receive, so a library import lands in an ambient source governing a module another build compiles without that library, and that build stops on the ambient source

arms.name: M-HOIST-RECEIVER-EVIDENCE-BLIND
arms.note: a receiver's own statements never vouch for the classpath entry it already compiles with, so every statement from a library is withheld wherever one governed module does not spell it

arms.name: M-HOIST-IMPLICIT-TIER-BLIND
arms.note: the language's implicit tier no longer vouches for a receiver, so an allow-listed using of a top-level std module is withheld from every directory where one module spells no other std statement

arms.name: M-HOIST-TIE-NEAREST-FIRST
arms.note: of two sites governing the same modules the nested one is weighed first, so a parent whose every module sits under one child takes the statement its child already took and one chain carries it twice

arms.name: M-COND-PARAM-ELSE-PLAIN
arms.note: the `#else` arm of a parameter region captures no per-element separator, so the comma it writes before `#end` is lost and that arm compiles two parameters with nothing between them

arms.name: M-COND-PARAM-ELSEIF-PLAIN
arms.note: an `#elseif` arm of a parameter region captures no per-element separator, so the comma it writes before the next directive is lost

arms.name: M-ELIDED-GAP-HARD
arms.note: every gap the source left without a separator is a forced line break again, so a parameter list that fits breaks after `#end`

arms.name: M-REGION-GLUED
arms.note: a region behind an elided separator glues onto the previous parameter's line, where `= false #if air, …` re-parses as a splice tail of the default value

arms.name: M-ELIDED-SEP-KEPT
arms.find: final elided: Bool = [for (k in from + 1...to) skipSepBefore(sepBeforeFlags, k)].contains(true);
arms.note: a fill run packs with one uniform separator, so a gap the source left comma-less gains a comma beside the one its region already wrote

arms.name: M-SINK-NEVER-SOUND
arms.note: no ambient statement is ever judged safe to send back to its readers, so the reverse direction proposes nothing and a statement one module reads stays in the source of a whole directory

arms.name: M-SINK-SHARE-BLIND
arms.find: if (candidate == null || reading.length == 0 || reading.length * PERCENT >= sink * governed.length) continue;
arms.note: the reader share is never read, so every ambient statement any module reads is sent back into its readers however many of them there are

arms.name: M-SINK-HYSTERESIS-OFF
arms.note: a sink threshold at or above the hoist one is honoured, so one share sits on both sides and a fix run moves the same statement into the ambient source and back out of it pass after pass

arms.name: M-SINK-RIVAL-BLIND
arms.find: if (imp.guarded || SymbolIndex.bindsAnyOf(imp, statement.names, ctx.publicTypes)) return false;
arms.note: a nearer ambient source binding the same name to another type is no rival, so the own copy a sink writes outranks it and the reader's name turns to the sunk statement's type

arms.name: M-SINK-OWN-RIVAL-BLIND
arms.note: a reader's own import of the same name is no rival, so the own copy a sink writes lands beside it and whichever sorts last takes the name

arms.name: M-SINK-USING-RANK-BLIND
arms.find: if (statement.isUsing && imp.kind == ImportKind.Using && ctx.contested(file, statement.path, imp.raw)) return false;
arms.note: another using in the reader's chain is no rival, so a sunk using turns own and outranks it, and every extension method both declare resolves to the sunk one

arms.name: M-EMPTY-AMBIENT-NEVER
arms.note: no ambient source is ever empty, so the file an emptying fix leaves behind stays on disk unreported

arms.name: M-EMPTY-AMBIENT-KEEPS
arms.note: a blank ambient source is reported and never deleted, so every emptying fix leaves its file behind

arms.name: M-FIX-REMOVE-IGNORED
arms.note: a slice that removes a file is staged and never committed, so a fix that deletes a file reports success and leaves it on disk

arms.name: M-FIX-REMOVE-NO-RESTORE
arms.find: if (original == null || files.exists(entry -> entry.file == path)) continue;
arms.note: the safe-pass revert restores the files the run still holds only, so a deletion the oracle rejected stays deleted and the tree the revert claims green does not compile

arms.name: M-FIX-AMBIENT-HELD
arms.note: an ambient source a pass rewrote stays in memory until the end of the run, so every later pass resolves the chain from the statements the source no longer carries

arms.name: M-SINK-WHOLE-FILE
arms.replace: edits: [{ span: new Span(0, (sourceOf[file] ?? '').length), text: textOf[file] ?? '' }]
arms.note: a sink rewrites each reader as one whole-file edit, so a cross-file rename another rule makes in that reader in the same pass overlaps it and one of the two is lost

arms.name: M-FIX-OVERLAP-BLIND
arms.note: the edits two cross-file fixes make in one file are merged unchecked, so where they overlap the later silently swallows the earlier and the run reports both as landed

arms.name: M-ENUM-CTOR-PARAMS-PLAIN
arms.note: an enum constructor's parameters capture no per-element separator, so every gap gets a comma and a region already ending on its own is followed by `#end, c:Int`

arms.name: M-TRAIL-AFTER-REGION
arms.note: a region ending the list takes the trailing comma again, which compiles to `, ,` once its branch is off

arms.name: M-TRAIL-AFTER-SEMI
arms.note: a class-notation structure field takes the trailing comma after its own `;`

arms.name: M-TRAIL-CASCADE-UNGATED
arms.note: the wrap cascade appends the trailing comma whatever the last item ends on

arms.name: M-TRAIL-FORCEMULTI-UNGATED
arms.note: a list laid out one item per line by a comment appends the trailing comma after a region ending it

arms.name: M-TRAIL-CALL-FORCEMULTI-UNGATED
arms.note: call arguments laid out one per line by a line comment append the trailing comma after a region ending them

arms.name: M-DOOR-TYPE-VALUE-NULL
arms.note: a type name read as a value carries no type, though 4.3.7 types it as its class or enum value

arms.name: M-DOOR-TYPE-VALUE-GENERIC
arms.note: a generic type read as a value is spelled without the arguments its value carries

arms.name: M-DOOR-TYPE-VALUE-SHADOWED-TRUE
arms.note: a name a member or a module constructor binds is typed as the type of that name

arms.name: M-DOOR-DECLARATION-NULL
arms.note: a local declaration carries no type, though 4.3.7 types it as the value it binds

arms.name: M-DOOR-DECLARATION-SEVERAL
arms.find: if (at == null || decl.children.exists(child -> continuations.contains(child.kind))) return null;
arms.note: a declaration binding several values is typed as its first

arms.name: M-DOOR-DECLARATION-WRITTEN-FIRST
arms.note: a declaration written with a type is typed by its initializer

arms.name: M-WALK-ASCRIBED-NULL
arms.note: an ascription `(e : T)` carries no type, though 4.3.7 types it as `T`

arms.name: M-WALK-SEGMENT-NULL
arms.note: a text segment of an interpolated string carries no type

arms.name: M-DOOR-USING-TYPES-BLIND
arms.note: beside a type a `using` brings no constructor, so a constructor a module it names may hold is taken for the type of that name

arms.name: M-DOOR-ANY-CONSTRUCTOR-BLIND
arms.note: a constructor of an enum nothing imports, which an expected type resolves first, is taken for the type of that name

arms.name: M-WALK-INTEGER-RANGE-FALSE
arms.find: return max != null && (digits.length > max.length || digits.length == max.length && digits > max);
arms.note: a decimal literal past the integer range is typed as the integer type, though 4.3.7 types `3000000000` as a `Float`

arms.name: M-WALK-INTEGER-SUFFIX-OPEN
arms.note: an integer literal with a suffix is typed as the integer type, though 4.3.7 types `1i64` as a `haxe.Int64` and `1u32` as a `UInt`

arms.name: M-TRAIL-REGION-UNDER-COMMENT
arms.note: a comment in front of a region ending the list hides the region, so the trailing-comma knob writes `#end,` again

arms.name: M-LEAD-BLOCK-COMMENT-END
arms.note: the scan resumes inside the closing `*/` of a leading block comment and reads its `/` as the item's first token

arms.name: M-CASCADE-LEAD-BREAKS
arms.note: the wrap cascade breaks after a block comment the source glued to its parameter, so the next write moves the parameter

arms.name: M-CLOSE-LOOP-LEAD-UNGLUED
arms.note: a closed trivia list records no glued leading comment, so a parameter's glued block comment is written on a line of its own

arms.name: M-NOWRAP-LEAD-IN-CASCADE
arms.note: a pure noWrap cascade takes an own-line comment and writes it after the previous parameter's comma

arms.name: M-CALL-SOURCE-TRAIL-OFF
arms.find: final tcExpr: Expr = trailingCommaExpr(branch, isTriviaStar ? postfixSourceTrailExpr() : null);
arms.note: a call laid out one argument per line drops the trailing comma its source wrote

arms.name: M-CALL-FLAT-SOURCE-TRAIL-OFF
arms.find: final flatTcExpr: Expr = c.isTriviaStar ? postfixSourceTrailExpr() : macro false;
arms.note: a call that stays on one line drops the trailing comma its source wrote

arms.name: M-USING-OFFER-OPEN
arms.note: a module whose every candidate rejects the receiver may still offer the access, so a `using` no access binds stays and a rival rejecting the receiver contests it

arms.name: M-USING-BOUND-ELSEWHERE
arms.note: an access another `using` provably binds first still counts as a use of every module accepting the receiver

arms.name: M-USING-STATIC-RECEIVER
arms.note: a static of the type a type expression names no longer binds first, so `Type.name(...)` keeps every `using` offering `name`

arms.name: M-USING-CONTEST-ANY
arms.note: any other `using` in scope contests the statement again, so redundant-import, hoist and sink refuse past a rival no access of the module shares

arms.name: M-UNUSED-USING-SELF-MENTION
arms.note: the declaring module's own declaration reads as a use of an ambient `using` of it, so a dead one is never reported

arms.name: M-USING-STATIC-SHADOW
arms.find: if (!ValueDoors.bindsNoValue(recv, typeName, span, fi, tree, _plugin.refShape(), _file, index)) return Unknown;
arms.note: a value spelled like a type — an inherited field, a module-level field, an imported static or constructor — reads as that type, so its static seems to bind and a `using` the value needs is deleted

arms.name: M-USING-FORWARD-DECIDED
arms.note: a `@:forward` abstract receiver is judged by its own type, so every extension its underlying type takes reads as rejecting it and the `using` that answers the forwarded access is deleted

arms.name: M-JSUL-SOURCE-ALWAYS-WRITTEN
arms.note: every source reads as written somewhere, so a parameter nothing writes stops collapsing into a later read

arms.name: M-JSUL-SOURCE-NEVER-WRITTEN
arms.note: no source reads as written, so a parameter assigned before or after the read, or from a closure, is inlined into a later statement that may see another value

arms.name: M-JSUL-LATER-HOLDER-ADJACENT-ONLY
arms.note: only the immediately following sibling is searched for the read, so a capture read several statements later is never found

arms.name: M-JSUL-LATER-DEFERRED-ALLOWED
arms.note: a later read inside a lambda declared between is accepted, moving the read into a closure

arms.name: M-JSUL-LATER-LOOP-BARRIER
arms.note: a loop on the path refuses a later read even though the invariant source makes every repetition read the same value

arms.name: M-JSUL-LATER-SOURCE-ANY-BINDER
arms.note: any resolved binder counts as invariant, so a catch binder outside the parameter and final-local whitelist is inlined into a later read

arms.name: M-JSUL-LATER-SOURCE-ANY-SCOPE
arms.find: if (fnSpan == null || binding.from < fnSpan.from || binding.to > fnSpan.to) return false;
arms.note: an outer function's parameter counts as owned by the nested function, so its capture is inlined into a later read past the whitelist

arms.name: M-JSUL-LATER-SOURCE-PARAMS-ONLY
arms.note: only parameters count as invariant, so a capture of a final local read several statements later stops collapsing

arms.name: M-SUPERTYPES-FIRST-WRITTEN-ONLY
arms.note: a declaration keeps only its first written supertype, so a class extending one superclass per #if branch is indexed under the first branch alone and prefer-inline inlines a method a later branch's subclass overrides

arms.name: M-OVERRIDDEN-DECLS-FIRST-LINK
arms.note: only the first written superclass link is walked, so an override whose superclass is named in a later #if branch binds to nothing and overridden-inline misses the inline method it overrides in that build

arms.name: M-OVERRIDDEN-INLINE-FIX-NONE
arms.note: the fix finds the overridden method's inline modifier and deletes nothing, so --fix leaves the override failing in every build that compiles it

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-INLINE-NONE
arms.find: return inlineMultilineBranch ? IfFirstLineExceeds(opt.lineWidth, broken, shapeNoWrap(items, ops)) : broken;
arms.note: the inline verdict is never read, so `ternaryMultilineBranch: inline` breaks the ternary like `break`

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-OPTION-IGNORED
arms.note: the option is not consulted, so `break` and an absent key keep a block-holding ternary glued like `inline`

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-NO-DESCENT
arms.note: a block below the branch top (a function argument, an object-literal value) is not found, so `inline` breaks those ternaries

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-PATH-UNSEARCHED
arms.note: the operands after the opening group are skipped along with it, so `[a, b].map(function() {…})` is not acted on

arms.name: M-TERNARY-MLB-NO-WIDTH-GUARD
arms.note: `inline` glues the ternary whatever the width, so a first line past the limit overflows

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-CONSTRUCTION-NULL
arms.note: a construction carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `new Box<Int>()` as `Box<Int>`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-CONSTRUCTION-AS-WRITTEN
arms.note: a construction leaving out arguments its type gives defaults is typed as written, `Pair<Int>`, though 4.3.7 completes it as `Pair<Int, Item>`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-ELEMENT-NULL
arms.note: an index access carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `a[0]` of an `Array<Int>` as `Int`

arms.name: M-INDEX-READ-FIRST
arms.note: an abstract's first read access is taken whatever key it casts, so a `String` key reads the `Int` access's element

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-OPERATOR-NULL
arms.note: an operator over core values carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `i + f` as `Float` and `s + i` as `String`

arms.name: M-COMPOUND-KEEPS-TARGET-FALSE
arms.note: a compound assignment carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `n += 1` of a `Null<Int>` as `Null<Int>`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-OVERLOAD-NULL
arms.note: an operator an abstract's overload takes carries no type, though 4.3.7 types it as the overload's return

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-INTERVAL-NULL
arms.note: the binder of a loop over `0...n` carries no type, though 4.3.7 types it as `Int`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-ENUM-VALUE-NULL
arms.note: an enum-abstract value read off its type carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `E.A` as `E`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-PARTS-NULL
arms.note: a literal nothing is expected of carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `[1, 2.5]` as `Array<Float>`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-EXPECTED-NULL
arms.note: a literal a type is expected of carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `[1, 2]` handed to a `Dynamic` parameter as `Array<Dynamic>`

arms.name: M-INDEX-HOST-PARENS-KEPT
arms.note: a parenthesized value carries no type, though parentheses change none

arms.name: M-MEMBER-READ-BRANCHES-FIRST
arms.find: if (live.exists(m -> m.typeSource != written || m.optional != first.optional)) return null;
arms.note: a member two `#if` branches write differently reads as the first branch's type, though a build of the other compiles the other

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-BRANCHES-NULL
arms.note: a conditional nothing is expected of carries no type, though 4.3.7 types `c ? 1 : 2.5` as `Float`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-DEFAULTS-UNWRITTEN
arms.note: a generic construction written with no argument is completed with its defaults, though 4.3.7 makes `new Def()` a monomorph the code binds later

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-UNIFIED-NULLABLE-DROPPED
arms.find: final nullable: Bool = parts.exists(p -> NominalTypes.outerNominalOf(p, c.chain.typeSyntax) == wrapper);
arms.note: a nullable number is unified with a bare one as the bare type, though 4.3.7 types `[n, 1]` of a `Null<Int>` as `Array<Null<Int>>`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-OPTIONAL-FIELD-BARE
arms.note: a written optional field is read as its declared type, though 4.3.7 types `b: 2` for `?b: Int` as `b: Null<Int>`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-DYNAMIC-FIELD-LITERAL
arms.find: if (literal) return spelled(declared, c) == shape.rawDynamicTypeName ? declared : typed;
arms.note: a literal written for a `Dynamic` field keeps its own type, though 4.3.7 types the field as `Dynamic`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-MAP-UNDER-DYNAMIC
arms.find: if (!object && node.children.exists(e -> e.kind == shape.mapLiteralEntryKind)) return null;
arms.note: a map literal under `Dynamic` is typed as an array of it, though 4.3.7 types it as a `haxe.ds.Map`

arms.name: M-OVERLOAD-GUARDED-SOURCE-ORDER
arms.note: the index order is taken for the source order, so an unguarded overload listed before a `#if` one the compiler tries first is picked

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-NULLABLE-KEEPS-OWN
arms.note: a class instance written for an optional field of its class is read as `Null<C>`, though 4.3.7 types `k: it` for `?k: Item` as `k: Item`

arms.name: M-COMPOSED-NULLABLE-ABSTRACT-DECIDED
arms.find: return decl != null && (decl.type.isAnonStruct || objects.exists(decl.type.kind)) ? true : null;
arms.note: every declared type is taken as nullable, so an abstract over `Int` written for an optional field keeps its type, though 4.3.7 types it `Null<A>`

arms.name: M-HOIST-BUILDS-UNASKED
arms.note: the run's declared builds are never asked which files each parses, so a receiver no statement of its own vouches for withholds a statement every build reading it already reads

arms.name: M-HOIST-BUILD-WITHOUT-MODULE-IGNORED
arms.note: a build that parses a receiver but not the statement's module no longer withholds the statement, so the ambient source stops that build on an import it cannot resolve

arms.name: M-HOIST-UNPARSED-RECEIVER-WITHHELD
arms.note: a receiver no declared build parses is read as parsed by a build that lacks the statement's module, so a statement is withheld from a directory holding code no build compiles

arms.name: M-DEFINES-PARSED-DROPPED
arms.note: a probed build names no file it parses, so every module it reads looks compiled by none of the builds

arms.name: M-MOVE-MEMBER-INTERP-SIBLING-PREFIXED
arms.note: a sibling read through a braceless `$name` interpolation gets the prefix as text before the `$`, changing the string

arms.name: M-MOVE-MEMBER-DEST-SHADOW-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a qualified reference landing inside the destination drops its qualifier even where a binder of the member's name would capture it

arms.name: M-INLINE-METHOD-SHADOW-PARTIAL
arms.note: the shadow check reads only parameters, local declarations and local functions, so a loop, catch or case binder of a parameter's name is substituted through

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOC-REGION-OWNER-UNREAD
arms.note: a doc above a conditional-compilation region resolves to the region, which has no name, so the guard watches nothing

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOC-ORPHAN-UNCHECKED
arms.note: deleting the last documented member leaves its doc above the closing brace, documenting nothing

arms.name: M-JSUL-LATER-LEADING-COMMENT-IGNORED
arms.note: the later-read fix deletes a capture under an own-line comment, which then documents whatever statement followed it

arms.name: M-MOVE-MEMBER-REIFICATION-BARED
arms.note: a qualified reference inside a macro reification lands bare, and binds wherever the macro is called

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOC-NESTED-REGION-UNREAD
arms.note: the descent stops at a region's first child when that child is itself a region, so a doc above nested regions is watched against the inner region, which has no name

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOC-REGION-SIBLINGS-INNER
arms.note: a doc's owner inside a region is compared against its siblings in the region, so deleting the whole region hands the doc to the next declaration as if renamed

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOC-EMPTY-REGION-OWNS
arms.note: a region that declares nothing is read as the doc's owner, so emptying the documented region hands the doc to the next declaration as if renamed

arms.name: M-REACH-STORED-UNREAD
arms.find: if (noOracle) return withStoredBuilds(resolution, oracles, reflective, holders);
arms.note: a run that compiles nothing never reads the builds an oracle run stored, so it knows no build and the alias branch no build takes is read again

arms.name: M-REACH-STORE-OFF
arms.replace: if (before == null || builds == null || oracles.length > 0) return;
arms.note: the builds an oracle run probed are never stored, so the next run that compiles nothing knows no build

arms.name: M-REACH-KEY-UNCHECKED
arms.find: return now == null || now.key != text(record['key']) ? null : buildsOf(record);
arms.note: a stored record is read under whatever fingerprint the input hashes to now, so builds probed of a source since edited answer for it

arms.name: M-REACH-GENERATION-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a generated hxml whose declared input changed still keys the stored builds, though the oracle run would generate it again

arms.name: M-REACH-LIBRARY-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a stored library source is read back whatever it holds now, so an edited file outside the fingerprint answers as the one the build compiled

arms.name: M-REACH-HASHED-UNCHECKED
arms.find: for (i in 0...oracles.length) if (!OracleCache.readsHashed(key.bases[i], configurations[i].parsed, key.hashed[i])) return;
arms.replace: for (i in 0...oracles.length) if (false && !OracleCache.readsHashed(key.bases[i], configurations[i].parsed, key.hashed[i])) return;
arms.note: a build that parsed a file the fingerprint did not hash — in a dot directory, past the walk's depth, outside every root — is stored, and an edit to that file is answered by the old build

arms.name: M-ORACLE-VERDICT-READS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a verdict whose compile read a file the fingerprint did not hash is stored, so an edit to that file is answered by the old verdict with no compile

arms.name: M-REACH-RECORD-SHAPE-UNCHECKED
arms.find: return items != null && items.foreach(item -> item is String) ? cast items : null;
arms.replace: return items != null ? cast items : null;
arms.note: a record's string lists are read whatever they hold, so a define that is no string reaches the builds

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-PATH-BLIND
arms.note: scrub-guard stops reading paths against the private roots, so a client file path named in the tree or in a pushed range passes the guard silently

arms.name: M-HOIST-UNKNOWN-BUILDS-GUESSED
arms.note: a project that declared its build list complete and whose builds the run does not know falls back on classpath evidence, so `--fix --no-oracle` writes an ambient statement into a directory a build of that list compiles without the statement's module

arms.name: M-HOIST-HELD-UNSAID
arms.note: a proof that held for want of the declared builds holds silently, so a run that hoists nothing reads as a tree with nothing to hoist

arms.name: M-REACH-COMPLETE-FOLLOWS-LIST
arms.note: a nested document naming a compilerOracle list of its own inherits the completeness its ancestor declared for another list, so the reach analysis reads a partial list as every build the project ships

arms.name: M-HOIST-MIXED-LISTS-GUESSED
arms.note: a run over paths whose configs name different oracle lists, one of them declared complete, carries no hold, so hoist-common-import falls back on classpath evidence and `--fix` writes an ambient statement a build of the declared list cannot resolve

arms.name: M-HELD-NOTE-LOST-WITH-FACTS
arms.note: the scope an oracle run hands its checks drops the hold, so a run whose declared builds did not answer falls back on classpath evidence and says nothing

arms.name: M-MERMAID-ENCODE-DROPPED
arms.note: an `@:encode` terminal is written as its decoded value, so a Mermaid label holding a quote or a pipe comes out bare and the writer's output no longer parses back to the AST it was given

arms.name: M-MERMAID-PLAIN-LT-RAW
arms.note: a plain label's `<` is written raw, so Mermaid reads it as markup: `Array<String>` loses its tag-shaped half and `<b>` renders bold

arms.name: M-MERMAID-PLAIN-AMP-RAW
arms.note: a plain label's `&` is written raw, so the text `"` renders as a quote and an escape written after a raw `&` completes a reference that re-reads as markup

arms.name: M-MERMAID-TICK-UNESCAPED
arms.note: a quoted label opening with a backtick is written as a markdown string opener, and a backtick inside a markdown string closes it early

arms.name: M-MERMAID-CODEPOINT-UNBOUNDED
arms.find: return code == null || code < 1 || code > MAX_CODE_POINT || (code >= SURROGATE_FIRST && code <= SURROGATE_LAST) ? null : code;
arms.note: a numeric code outside Unicode reaches String.fromCharCode and throws a RangeError, and a surrogate decodes to half a character

arms.name: M-MERMAID-INLINE-TAKES-PREFIX
arms.note: a bare solid-edge label stops at markup without asking for its closing link, so plain takes the prefix before the space and `A -- a < b --> E` no longer parses

arms.name: M-MERMAID-NUMERIC-REF-RAW
arms.note: markup writes a numeric HTML reference raw, and Mermaid, which turns every `#\w+;` into a reference whatever precedes it, renders `<` as `&<`

arms.name: M-MERMAID-CODE-ALPHABET-NARROW
arms.note: a code name may not hold `_`, so plain text `#a_b;` is written unescaped and Mermaid renders it as the reference `&a_b;`

arms.name: M-MERMAID-DOTTED-TEXT-TAKES-DOTS
arms.note: a bare dotted-edge label takes every dot but the one before the `-`, so `-. text ..->` reads the label `text .` where Mermaid's lexer closes the link at `..->`

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-TAIL-BLIND
arms.note: a path is read only as a whole, so a private path behind a longer lead (another checkout, a project directory) passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-ABSOLUTE-BLIND
arms.note: a token may not start after a `/` again, so a private path inside an absolute, home-relative or URL path passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-DOTTED-BLIND
arms.note: a dotted name names nothing, so a private module spelled as a package path passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-ROOT-MODULE-BLIND
arms.note: no name counts as compound, so a private module directly under a source root passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-DIRECTORY-BLIND
arms.note: a path with no extension names nothing, so a private directory passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-BACKSLASH-BLIND
arms.note: a backslash is no separator, so a private path written with backslashes passes the guard

arms.name: M-SCRUB-PRIVATE-ESCAPE-BLIND
arms.note: a backslash never opens a string escape, so a private dotted path glued to a `\t` in a quoted fixture passes the guard
